featured_reviews.review_text:
We are deeply grateful that my father’s CABG surgery on was successful and truly appreciate the expertise and care provided by the surgeon and medical team during the procedure. The doctor’s professionalism gave our family a great sense of confidence during a very difficult time.
However, our experience with the support staff, particularly the RMO in the ICU and cardiac care unit, was extremely disappointing and distressing. During my father’s stay in the ICU, it was a daily struggle to even speak to him, despite the hospital having provided a dedicated contact number and specified calling hours for relatives. Calls would often go unanswered, and obtaining even basic updates became unnecessarily difficult.
More concerning was the attitude and behavior displayed toward patient relatives. At such a sensitive and emotionally exhausting time, families look for empathy, communication, and basic courtesy. Instead, interactions often felt rude, dismissive, and as though allowing us to see or inquire about our father was being treated as a personal favor rather than part of professional patient care.
We fully understand that working in an ICU environment is demanding and stressful, and we respect the pressures healthcare professionals face daily. However, compassion and respectful communication are fundamental aspects of healthcare, especially in critical care settings where families are already under immense emotional strain.
We hope the hospital administration takes this feedback seriously and ensures that staff dealing with patients’ families are trained not only in clinical responsibilities but also in empathy, communication, and professionalism. A successful surgery alone does not define a family’s hospital experience — humane treatment and respectful interaction matter equally.
Also, please do not respond with the usual “call this number for further clarification regarding your case,” because in reality, the calls are rarely answered and relatives are left helpless despite following the exact process advised by the hospital. Publishing contact numbers and designated calling hours serves no purpose if there is no accountability in responding to anxious family members seeking updates about critically ill patients.
Families dealing with loved ones in the ICU are already emotionally overwhelmed. The least they deserve is timely communication, basic courtesy, and humane treatment — not indifference and unnecessary hostility.
